summary: Per-inference forensic ledger export and penetration-test correlation playback request
description: Customer (Quartz Analytics) requests a structured, per-inference audit ledger suitable for a live penetration test and subsequent forensic playback. Requirements: 1) each inference event must include request_id, tenant_id, session_id, model_version_tag, model_weights_sha256, gpu_job_id, node_hostname, start_ts, end_ts, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, billing_token_unit, and optionally truncated prompt hash. 2) events must be exportable as NDJSON and a compact CSV mapping for Splunk HEC with an example HEC payload. 3) redaction rules: automatic jurisdiction-aware redaction flags (EU/UK) with ability to mask PII fields using tenant-provided HMAC pepper (customer-supplied secret) and an audit of the HMAC key rotation. 4) signed manifest for each export (RFC3161 timestamp + sig using Redwood export key) and resumable playback tokens so customer can replay a timeframe and validate chain. 5) ability to correlate inference events to ephemeral service principal keys and session tokens used during the pen-test (they will supply timeline and list of suspected SPNs). They additionally ask for a short recommended rollout/playback runbook and best-practice configuration for retention and signed-manifest verification.
impact: Customer is conducting an internal pen-test and needs reliable provenance and a mapping from suspicious inference spikes to the exact service identities and GPU job traces. This is blocking their security sign-off and SOC evidence package; could delay go-live for a regulated feature.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Quartz team will run a scripted burst test that calls gpt-redwood-v1 with long context (20k tokens) across 20 concurrent sessions. 2) They will mark timestamps T0-T3 and provide request_ids. 3) Support should produce an on-demand export for 2026-03-09T23:50 -> 2026-03-10T00:30 including all per-inference fields and a signed manifest. 4) Customer will attempt to replay using resume tokens and validate HMAC pseudonym mappings.
logs: Support pulled serving-runtime traces for the requested window: found GPU job ids node-az1-gpu-07 (job 78910) and node-az1-gpu-09 (job 78912). Token accounting shows bursts aligning to request_ids prefixed with qz-pt-*. No server-side 5xx recorded, but several long tail latencies > 2.5s for generation-at-scale. Collected sample NDJSON lines and anonymized them and attached in internal bundle (see related_github_prs).
investigation_notes: - Initial triage: mapping exists in runtime logs between request_id -> gpu_job_id and host. - Audit pipeline currently emits a per-request event but lacks model_weights_sha256 and gpu_job_id in Splunk HEC mapping. - HMAC pseudonymization supports tenant salt but not external pepper rotation audit; engineering needs to add pepper-injection and rotation metadata to manifest. - Signing/export codepath supports RFC3161 stamps but per-export resumable resume_token is not yet exposed to customers; requires small API addition. - Proposed short-term workaround: generate NDJSON with additional fields server-side and deliver via SFTP and provide manual RFC3161-signed manifest. Long-term: add HEC schema and resume-token API.
resolution: Workarounds provided: (1) On 2026-03-11 Support produced a one-off NDJSON export for the requested window containing the extended fields and delivered via SFTP. (2) Provided a Splunk HEC example payload and a Python script that wraps NDJSON -> HEC batching with the customer's field mapping. (3) Delivered an RFC3161 timestamped manifest signed by the compliance exports key. Engineering action items: ADD-1149 (add model_weights_sha256 to standard audit events), ADD-1150 (expose resume_token and playback API), SEC-2201 (support pepper rotation audit entries). Follow-up: schedule a walkthrough with customer for 2026-03-15 to validate playback and HMAC verification.
